correctness.rationale: The squared Gaussian spectrogram at Hermite index j is e^(-x) x^j/j! for x=pi|z|^2, and integration over angle gives the radial measure dx. In particular 1-h replaces all three responses by their complements. For fixed mass p, crossing the thresholds -log(1-p) and -log p gives the lower disk and upper tail first-moment bounds: subtract the threshold times the matching mass, and the remaining integrand difference has fixed sign. Positivity away from the single threshold forces uniqueness on the two edges. At 0<p<1 the interval of mass p has e^(-a)=u, e^(-b)=u-p; its first moment is strictly decreasing in u with derivative log((u-p)/u), and its endpoint moments are precisely q_+ and q_-. At a strict interior pair the two distinct roots a,b are positive and finite. Subtracting the matching zero-th and first moments from the difference in r leaves one half the integral of (x-a)(x-b)(h-h_-), which equals the claimed absolute-value integrand everywhere by sign. It vanishes only for h=h_- almost everywhere. Complementation proves the analogous maximum identity and uniqueness; interpolation of these masks gives every intermediate r, and the edge masks and p=0,1 cases are already forced. The exponential antiderivative gives R. At p=q=1/2, independent 70-digit quadrature and root solving give a=0.435551673686811025..., b=1.917950871301904402..., and r_min=0.291158321988844511...; the last displayed digits of the approximate endpoints in the record differ by floating-point roundoff, without changing the result. See RESULT.md Steps 1–5 for exact replay and checker.py for inspected finite diagnostics only. The identities are interior only, and the claim concerns labelled responses for bounded radial masks, not ordered eigenvalues or fixed area.

evidence: The Koshevoy–Mosler support theorem allows general finite-first-moment vector laws; the lifted exponential parabola has finite first moments, with positive measure on each nonempty x-interval and zero measure at a finite set of roots. Lemma 3.1 already identifies the one-dimensional lift zonoid through its two tail-integral curves.

The inspected Dette–Schorning result admits unrestricted (in particular atomic) measures on a compact interval and is not itself the needed bounded-density theorem. The Gaussian localization papers compare different constraints/objectives: prescribed area and a single concentration objective, or ordered spectrum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general support theorem genuinely covers this admissible class and determines the exact body, not just a qualitative similarity. The competing moment-space and fixed-area spectral formulations are not the basis of the coverage.

evidence: For any score L=d·W the difference between the support value and the score of h in the proof of Eq. (2.2) is E[L_+-Lh]=E[|L||1_{L>0}-h|]. Equality forces the indicator off the score-zero set. On a fixed (p,q) slice take L=-(X-a)(X-b)/2 to expose the minimum r, and apply the complementary slice for the maximum. The affine terms cancel exactly, giving both recorded gap identities, not only bounds.

Use the linear scores from the same theorem to obtain the two tail bounds; fitting the positive interval of the quadratic score uses only e^(-a)-e^(-b)=p and the first moment. The scalar curve is strictly monotone by log((u-p)/u)<0, giving the complete domain of the parameter. Its exponential tail integrals give q_± and R; central symmetry and convex slicing supply the second endpoint and all intermediate r.

originality.rationale: The complete attainable body is exactly a classical lift zonoid, and both weighted identities are pointwise support losses in the proof of its general support theorem. The quadratic form and exponential inverse in this application follow by taking the sign of a quadratic and integrating three elementary moments; the paper of Koshevoy–Mosler need not separately list Gaussian channels for this coverage. The failure is for concrete implication by a prior exact theorem, not for inability to inspect some related moment literature.
residual_risks: Earlier more explicit exponential or Gaussian instances may exist. The Winkler full text was not accessible. Neither issue is needed to establish the concrete lift-zonoid implication.

value.rationale: Conditional Hermite calibration is a natural use of the formulas. But under the standard for exact invariants, the proposed result is the existing support theorem for a specific law, with direct score substitution, fitted endpoints and elementary exponential quadrature. Both stability identities are the same general pointwise slack, so they leave no separately supported novel stability claim after removing covered content. Practical convenience in this application does not supply a surviving mathematical finding for repair.
